## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Hive
where: HiveRepository (uses), src/persistence/repositories.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
private readonly items = new Map<string, Hive>();
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Hive Owner
where: TreatmentService (uses), src/business/treatmentService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
if (hive.ownerId !== ownerId) {
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are different concepts. A is the Hive entity itself: HiveRepository in src/persistence/repositories.ts stores it as `private readonly items = new Map<string, Hive>();`. B is the Hive Owner, the party who owns a hive. In src/business/treatmentService.ts it appears only as a reference held on a hive (`if (hive.ownerId !== ownerId) {`), and TreatmentService uses that check to confirm ownership. An owner is a person or account (a beekeeper), and a hive is a bee colony or box. The two are linked by an ownership relation, but they are not the same real-world thing under different names.
